documentationComparison.classification: explicit deviation from Local usage notes

documentationComparison.docs: Local names are case insensitive; second create errors.
documentationComparison.observed: Differently cased second create failed InternalFailure; differently cased DescribeTable returned ResourceNotFoundException, not alias access.
documentationComparison.classification: creation conflict agrees; exact failure and read asymmetry are additional engine facts

documentationComparison.docs: Without sharedDb, local access-key ID and region select separate files.
documentationComparison.observed: Same table name was created independently under another local access ID and another region; each isolated table scanned empty while primary contained data.

documentationComparison.docs: Local supports streams with shard behavior differing from AWS.
documentationComparison.observed: All four stream APIs succeeded; six INSERT/MODIFY records included real keys and old/new images. Same six records accessible after engine reopen.
documentationComparison.classification: agrees; native region ddblocal and account 999000999000 need owned metadata translation

documentationComparison.docs: Local does not support tagging or PITR.
documentationComparison.observed: TagResource, UpdateContinuousBackups, CreateBackup and ListBackups returned UnknownOperationException.
documentationComparison.classification: tags/PITR agree; native on-demand backup APIs not exposed by this build

runtimeSeamAssessment.classification: inference grounded in inspected repository patterns and executed engine calls
runtimeSeamAssessment.smallestSeam: A consumer-owned DynamoDB runtime taking the existing caller-owned *docker.Client plus immutable image, durable volume identity, endpoint/publication configuration and startup timeout. It owns image inspection, labeled volume/container lifecycle, API readiness, shutdown and removal; the shared client remains a generic Docker transport.
nativeEngineRequests: POST /volumes/create with ownership labels checked in returned object
POST /containers/create with dbPath volume and disableTelemetry command
DELETE /volumes/{owned-volume} only when storage is intentionally discarded
runtimeSeamAssessment.sharedTransportGap: compute/docker ContainerHostConfig currently has no PortBindings and ContainerConfig has no ExposedPorts or Hostname fields. A consumer-local request shape can express native loopback bindings without inventing a generalized service runtime. Existing JSON method accepts any request shape.
runtimeSeamAssessment.readiness: Require a successful signed native ListTables after log/TCP readiness; this experiment proved fresh named-volume permissions can otherwise leave a listening engine unable to open its DB. Initialize only the owned volume for image user dynamodblocal.
runtimeSeamAssessment.controlDataSplit: Keep AWS-facing table/index lifecycle, canonical ARNs, tags, billing/capacity/autoscaling metadata and unsupported control operations in the Go owner. Forward key/value, expressions, queries/scans, condition checks, transactions, PartiQL and stream data to the real engine; do not recreate evaluation/query logic.
runtimeSeamAssessment.namespace: Use stable synthetic alphanumeric engine access IDs for owned account namespaces and explicit region to leverage real DB separation; client-provided temporary access-key IDs must not select independent storage. Distinct AWS-facing table names differing only by case require case-safe stable physical identifiers. Such translation must cover nested batch/transaction maps and PartiQL table identifiers, not just top-level TableName; literal user data must not be rewritten.
runtimeSeamAssessment.streams: Native stream APIs are available on the same endpoint. Owner must map ddblocal/999000999000 ARNs, stream identifiers and record metadata to exposed account/region while retaining native records and cursor semantics.
runtimeSeamAssessment.backup: No native safe on-demand backup/restore API was exposed. No file copying or synthetic restore was attempted. Durable graceful reopen is proved, not live-copy consistency or crash durability.

uncertainties: No crash/power-loss durability, concurrent writers, maximum scale, TTL expiration timing or provisioned throttling enforcement experiment.
No live filesystem copy and no native restore attempt after backup API rejection; cannot claim any snapshot consistency guarantee.
